vanilla.irrigationNote: Protect from summer stress (Jan-May); keep basin mulched; ensure drainage in monsoon.

walnut.name: Walnut
walnut.irrigationNote: Stress during nut filling reduces kernel weight.

watermelon.name: Watermelon
watermelon.irrigationNote: Water at base only; keep leaves dry. Reduce water near harvest for sweetness (melons).

wheat.name: Wheat
wheat.criticalStages: Crown root initiation (20-25 DAS), jointing, flowering, milk/grain filling
wheat.irrigationNote: Avoid irrigation in strong wind after heading (lodging). Stop irrigation at physiological maturity.

winegrapes.name: Wine grapes
winegrapes.irrigationNote: Regulate water during berry development; withhold before pruning as per crop calendar.

yam.name: Yam
yam.irrigationNote: Waterlogging rots roots/tubers. Stop irrigation 10-15 days before harvest.

yerbamate.name: Yerba mate
yerbamate.irrigationNote: Provide irrigation through summer; mulch basin; maintain drainage in monsoon.

zinnia.name: Zinnia
zinnia.irrigationNote: Keep foliage and flowers dry; many are grown under protection.

PM.name: Powdery mildew
PM.scout: White powdery patches on upper leaf surface

DM.name: Downy mildew / white rust
DM.scout: Yellow angular patches above, grey-purple growth below leaf
DM.etl: First symptoms; preventive when trigger HIGH

RUST.name: Rust
RUST.scout: Orange/brown pustules that rub off as powder

EB.name: Early blight / Alternaria leaf spot
EB.scout: Brown spots with concentric rings, older leaves first

LB.name: Late blight
LB.scout: Water-soaked dark patches, white growth under leaf in morning
LB.etl: Preventive when trigger HIGH - spreads in days

ANTH.name: Anthracnose / fruit rot
ANTH.scout: Sunken dark lesions on fruit, twigs or leaves

BLAST.name: Blast
BLAST.scout: Spindle/eye-shaped spots with grey centre; neck turns black
BLAST.etl: Leaf blast on 2-5% leaves or neck blast risk at heading

SHB.name: Sheath blight
SHB.scout: Oval grey-green lesions on sheath near water line

BB.name: Bacterial blight / canker
BB.scout: Water-soaked streaks/spots turning yellow-brown; corky cankers on fruit

PHY.name: Phytophthora rot (bud/fruit/foot rot, gummosis)
PHY.scout: Rotting at collar, bud, pod or fruit; gum oozing; leaf fall in monsoon

SCAB.name: Scab
SCAB.scout: Olive-brown velvety spots on leaves and fruit
SCAB.etl: Preventive from green tip to fruit set when wet

SIG.name: Sigatoka leaf spot
SIG.scout: Yellow streaks turning to brown spots with grey centre

WILT.name: Wilt / root & collar rot (soil-borne)
WILT.scout: Plants droop in day, yellow, brown vascular tissue; rot at collar

APH.name: Aphids
APH.scout: Colonies on tender shoots/under leaves; sticky honeydew

WF.name: Whitefly
WF.scout: Tiny white flies under leaves; leaf curl/yellow mosaic
WF.etl: 5-8 adults per leaf (virus vector - act early)

THR.name: Thrips
THR.scout: Silvery streaks, leaf curl upward, scarring on fruit

JAS.name: Jassids / leafhoppers / hoppers
JAS.scout: Leaf edges yellow then burn (hopper burn), insects move sideways

MITE.name: Mites
MITE.scout: Fine webbing, bronze/grey speckling, leaf curling down

MB.name: Mealybug
MB.scout: White cottony masses on stems, fruit, roots

SCALE.name: Scale insects
SCALE.scout: Hard or soft scales on twigs and leaves; sooty mould

BPH.name: Brown planthopper
BPH.scout: Hoppers at base of tillers; circular drying patches (hopper burn)

FB.name: Fruit / boll / head borer (Helicoverpa)
FB.scout: Bored fruit/flowers with holes and frass
FB.etl: 1 larva per plant or 5% fruit damage

SB.name: Stem / shoot borer
SB.scout: Dead heart / dead shoot, bore holes with frass

FAW.name: Fall armyworm
FAW.scout: Window-pane feeding, ragged holes, sawdust-like frass in whorl

SPOD.name: Leaf-eating caterpillar (Spodoptera / semilooper / hairy caterpillar)
SPOD.scout: Skeletonised or eaten leaves, egg masses under leaves

DBM.name: Diamondback moth
DBM.scout: Small windows/holes in leaves, small green larvae wriggle when touched

FF.name: Fruit fly
FF.scout: Oozing puncture marks on fruit, maggots inside, fruit drop
FF.etl: Trap catch rising / first punctured fruit

SFB.name: Shoot & fruit borer
SFB.scout: Wilted shoot tips, bore holes in fruit

PBW.name: Pink bollworm
PBW.scout: Rosette flowers, bored green bolls, stained lint
PBW.etl: 8 moths/trap/night for 3 nights or 10% infested bolls

TMB.name: Tea mosquito bug
TMB.scout: Black necrotic spots on tender shoots, inflorescence drying

PALM.name: Palm beetles (rhinoceros beetle / red palm weevil)
PALM.scout: V-shaped cuts on fronds, holes in crown, oozing brown liquid

CBB.name: Coffee berry borer
CBB.scout: Pin hole at berry tip, powder inside

WG.name: White grub / soil insects
WG.scout: Plants wilt and pull out easily; C-shaped grubs in soil
WG.etl: 1 grub per sq m / beetles at first monsoon rain

TERM.name: Termites
TERM.scout: Plants dry from roots, mud tubes
TERM.etl: Any patch damage in dry spell

products.name: Wettable sulphur 80% WDG
products.note: Do not spray above 32°C or within 15 days of oil sprays

products.name: Copper oxychloride 50% WP
products.note: Organic: copper is restricted - check certifier limit

products.name: Copper hydroxide 77% WP
products.note: Organic: copper is restricted - check certifier limit

products.name: Copper oxychloride 50% WP
products.note: Streptomycin + tetracycline is banned for agricultural use in India - do not recommend

products.name: Bordeaux mixture 1%
products.dose: 10 g copper sulphate + 10 g lime per L
products.note: Pre-monsoon and mid-monsoon; also paste on trunk base

products.name: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (drench)
products.dose: 2.5 g/L, 1 L per sq m bed

products.name: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL
products.note: Toxic to bees - not during flowering hours

products.name: Lecanicillium (Verticillium) lecanii 1.15% WP
products.note: Plus fish oil rosin soap 25 g/L

products.name: Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki
products.note: Spray in evening on young larvae

products.name: Trichogramma egg cards
products.note: Plus pheromone traps 5/acre; remove dead hearts

products.name: Pheromone traps (cue-lure / methyl eugenol)
products.note: Cue-lure for cucurbits; methyl eugenol for mango/guava

products.name: Bait spray: Malathion 50% EC + jaggery
products.dose: 2 ml + 10 g per L, spot spray
products.note: Spot spray only, not whole canopy

products.name: Field sanitation
products.dose: Collect & bury fallen fruit 0.5 m deep

products.name: Neem oil (Azadirachtin 1500 ppm)
products.note: Remove mined leaves; yellow sticky traps

products.name: Pheromone traps / mating disruption (PB rope)
products.dose: 5 traps/acre; PB rope as per label

products.name: Leaf-axil filling: neem cake + sand
products.dose: 250 g neem cake + 250 g sand per palm, top 3 axils

products.name: Metarhizium anisopliae (manure pits)
products.dose: As per label in breeding sites

products.name: Metarhizium anisopliae (with FYM)
products.dose: 2 kg in 100 kg FYM per acre
products.note: Light traps at first monsoon rains

products.name: Fipronil 5% SC (with irrigation)
products.dose: 2 ml/L soil drench / 1 L per acre in irrigation

products.name: Neem cake + Metarhizium
products.dose: 100 kg neem cake/acre with 2 kg Metarhizium

sprayRules.note: Koleroga (fruit rot): Bordeaux 1% before monsoon and repeat after 40-45 days.
Aphids spread bunchy top virus - uproot and destroy infected plants.
Whitefly spreads yellow mosaic virus - uproot infected plants.
Quick wilt (foot rot): drench and spray Bordeaux at monsoon onset.
Capsule rot: Bordeaux at monsoon onset.
Thrips and mites cause leaf curl - check which pest before choosing product.
Citrus canker: spray after new flush and after rain.
Remove and burn dead palms and breeding sites.
Spray before and after monsoon.
Direct spray into the whorl; early morning or evening.
Bt cotton: pink bollworm is resistant to Bt toxin - follow pheromone monitoring.
Whitefly spreads leaf curl virus - act at 5-8 adults/leaf.
Highest risk 0-45 days after October pruning.
Whitefly spreads yellow mosaic virus - uproot infected plants.
Citrus canker: spray after new flush and after rain.
Protect panicles at emergence and full bloom.
Mango hopper: spray at panicle emergence, not in full bloom.
Whitefly spreads yellow vein mosaic - uproot infected plants.
Add sticker; thrips hide in leaf folds.
Aphids spread ringspot virus - use barrier crop and remove infected plants.
Bacterial blight (oily spot): prune infected parts, spray after pruning and after rain.
Late blight can destroy crop in a week - spray preventively when trigger is HIGH.
Mites spread sterility mosaic - control mites early.
Stop nitrogen top-dress when BLB appears; drain field.
Avoid synthetic pyrethroids - they cause BPH resurgence.
Abnormal leaf fall: prophylactic spray before monsoon.
Leafhoppers spread phyllody - uproot infected plants.
Early shoot borer (0-90 days) and top borer - granules in soil with irrigation.
Highest risk 0-45 days after October pruning.
Blister blight in monsoon - copper + systemic per Tea Board advisory.
Late blight risk in cool, foggy weather.
Yellow rust favours 10-20°C - check northern hills/plains in Jan-Feb.
Highest risk 0-45 days after October pruning.

irrigationMethods.name: Drip
irrigationMethods.bestTime: Early morning; split into 2 pulses on hot days
irrigationMethods.avoid: Running when soil is already wet; clogged emitters
irrigationMethods.fertilizerMethod: Fertigation: dissolve water-soluble fertilizer, inject in middle 1/2 of run, flush 10 min

irrigationMethods.name: Micro irrigation / micro-sprinkler
irrigationMethods.avoid: Strong wind; flowering of disease-prone crops

irrigationMethods.name: Sprinkler
irrigationMethods.avoid: Wind > 15 km/h; afternoon; flowering of crops prone to foliar disease (see Crops → Avoid irrigation)
irrigationMethods.fertilizerMethod: Broadcast fertilizer first, then run sprinkler 30-45 min to wash in

irrigationMethods.name: Flood / surface (border, basin)
irrigationMethods.avoid: Before heavy rain; waterlogging-sensitive crops (pulses, vegetables)

irrigationMethods.name: Furrow
irrigationMethods.fertilizerMethod: Side-dress fertilizer in furrow then irrigate

irrigationMethods.name: Rainfed
irrigationMethods.fertilizerMethod: Apply fertilizer only when soil is moist (after rain)
